summary: Initial compliance and data residency discovery for BankCorp evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Primary concerns: EU data residency/GDPR, financial services logging retention and redaction, HIPAA applicability for certain product lines, KMS/HSM integration, VPC/private deployment network controls, and audit log availability. BankCorp leans toward Dedicated but needs Private for certain regulated workloads; wants benchmark and TCO comparison.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
Network controls - VPC, private control plane, on-prem options
Next steps: docs and benchmark scheduling
transcript: 00:00 Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro from our side — I'm Alex, AE for this account, with Priya our solutions engineer. 00:08 Marta (BankCorp): Hi, Marta here, Head of Cloud Security at BankCorp. We pulled in Tom and Sanjay. 00:14 Tom: Morning. 00:16 Priya (Redwood SE): Hi all, thanks for the time. we'll keep this focused on data residency and compliance so we can understand where Redwood fits. 00:25 Alex: Quick agenda — 1) current stack and constraints, 2) compliance needs (GDPR, HIPAA, financial regs), 3) hosting options we offer, 4) next steps. sound good? 00:36 Marta: Yes. to start, our prod workloads are primarily in AWS us-east and eu-west for EEA customers. we have strict EEA-only data residency needs for certain products — if data comes from an EU customer, it must remain in eu region and logs retained in-region. 00:52 Sanjay: Also, we have a regulated payments product that potentially touches PAN and masked data; we treat some telemetry as sensitive, so logging policy is more restrictive. 01:03 Priya: Okay, thanks. When you say logs retained in-region, is that for raw transcripts or for metadata? 01:09 Marta: Both. we need to ensure raw transcripts and any embeddings generated from EU customer data stay in the EU. we also need controls on redaction and retention windows. 01:20 Alex: Understood. quick overview of our modes — Hosted (Redwood API) is multi-region with regional tenancy for EEA, Hosted supports EU-only data processing when configured and we can sign data processing addendums; Dedicated gives you reserved capacity in a region or region set and isolates compute; Private gives you a customer-managed control plane — VPC or on-prem — full network isolation and customer key control. 01:45 Tom: For Private, does control plane still touch metadata? we need to avoid cross-region copies of logs. 01:52 Priya: With Private deployments the control plane can be run in your VPC or on-prem. logs and transcripts can be configured to remain on your side. there are modes where we ship a private control plane image. note there's an operational tradeoff — you manage upgrades or we do update coordination. 02:08 Marta: Right. and what about KMS integration — we have a bank HSM and strict key separation policies. 02:14 Alex: We integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSMs. for Dedicated we support BYOK via AWS KMS and for Private we support direct HSM integration. key usage logging can be forwarded to your audit systems. 02:26 Sanjay: Do you have SOC 2 and ISO attestation docs? we'll need them for procurement. 02:30 Alex: Yes — SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 and GDPR DPA template. I'll send those after the call. 02:37 Priya: Also, for HIPAA — do you process PHI? we have customers who sign BAAs; Redwood can support HIPAA controls on Private and Dedicated deployments with appropriate agreements. 02:48 Marta: Some lines of business may process PHI if we embed medical payment flows; it's not our main product but it's a potential. so HIPAA readiness matters. 02:55 Tom: latency is a concern. Hosted is easiest but we need sub-200ms token latencies for customer-facing flows; do you have performance profiles for EU regions? 03:05 Priya: Yes, we maintain per-region performance profiles. Dedicated gives you predictable p99 latencies; Hosted can be tuned but shared tenancy may have variance. for strict SLAs Dedicated or Private is recommended. 03:17 Sanjay: logging retention policies — we have regulatory requirements to keep logs for seven years for certain financial events. can you support longer retention and immutable audit trails? 03:29 Alex: We can configure retention; with Hosted we provide retention options but long-retention of raw transcripts in EU might be limited by our standard retention tiers — Dedicated or Private allows you to own retention entirely. 03:41 Marta: Are there any issues with embeddings? we need embeddings created from EU data to never leave EU. 03:47 Priya: For Dedicated or Private we can ensure model exec and embedding generation are pinned to EU and that cached keys and embeddings remain in-region. Hosted has an EU-specific tenancy option; we'll need to include that in the DPA. 03:58 Jenna (BankCorp): For Private, what's the rough TCO delta vs Dedicated? our infra team is sensitive to ops overhead. 04:05 Alex: There's ops overhead for Private; Dedicated is a middle ground — managed by Redwood but isolated compute. Private is higher capex/ops but gives you full control for compliance. we'll put together a TCO comparison. 04:18 Sanjay: Regarding encryption in transit and at rest — do you support client-side encryption or tokenization of PII before sending? 04:25 Priya: We support TLS 1.2/1.3 in transit and at-rest encryption using customer-managed keys. client-side tokenization is possible — many customers pre-process PII before sending. we can help design that pattern. 04:36 Tom: Auditability — we need detailed audit logs with who accessed what, key usage, model versioning and prompt lineage. 04:44 Priya: We emit extensive audit logs that include request metadata, model version, route, and user IDs. with Dedicated/Private you can route logs to your SIEM and enable SAML-based auditing. 04:55 Marta: Does Redwood keep raw transcripts for any hosted debug purposes? we need assurances about no retention beyond configured windows. 05:02 Alex: By default we retain for debugging a short period but we can disable or shorten retention. Contractually we can guarantee retention bounds and provide options to redact or disable storage. 05:13 Sanjay: Can you support in-region logging for third-party monitoring vendors? we can't have cross-border log shipping without a DPIA. 05:21 Priya: You can route logs to your in-region SIEM and we can avoid shipping logs out. Hosted customers may need additional DPA clauses. 05:30 Tom: On the legal side, procurement will want DPA, subprocessors list, and data flow diagrams. 05:36 Alex: We'll provide DPA and subprocessors. I'll attach a standard subprocessors list; for Dedicated/Private we have fewer third parties. 05:44 Marta: For HIPAA, is there a BAA? 05:46 Alex: Yes — we can execute a BAA but typically only for Private/Dedicated where you control PHI handling. Hosted is possible in some cases but we need to review. 05:56 Jenna: Network egress — we've had issues where managed services still route telemetry to vendor endpoints in US. what guarantees for EU-only routing? 06:05 Priya: We provide region-scoped endpoints and network policies; Private ensures no egress. Dedicated can be configured with regional endpoints and IP allow lists to restrict routing. 06:17 Sanjay: Encryption key rotation policies? we require quarterly rotation and escrow. 06:23 Alex: We support customer-managed rotation schedules via KMS; escrow arrangements are possible for keys held in HSMs, we can discuss specifics with your cryptography team. 06:34 Marta: Incident response and breach notification times? 06:38 Alex: We have an IR process with notification SLAs; will include in security pack. 06:42 Tom: Can we run a performance benchmark in our environment to simulate token load and measure latency and cost per 1M tokens? 06:49 Priya: Absolutely — we'll set up a benchmark plan. typically SE-led, we provision a dedicated job and coordinate with your infra to route traffic to Dedicated/Private endpoints. 06:58 Sanjay: A couple of very specific asks — 1) show that embeddings from EU never leave region, 2) show exact audit log schema and retention controls, 3) provide a diagram of the private control plane network flow. 07:12 Alex: Good checklist. we'll deliver those three items. 07:16 Marta: Any blockers you foresee? 07:19 Priya: No blockers technical at this stage; it's mostly procurement and legal alignment. 07:23 Jenna: For the procurement team, can you provide pricing ranges for Dedicated vs Private? we don't need exact numbers but order-of-magnitude. 07:31 Alex: We'll provide ballpark TCO and a sample pricing sheet; exact pricing requires sizing. 07:36 Tom: On data subject requests under GDPR — if a customer requests deletion, how do we ensure transcripts and embeddings are removed? 07:44 Priya: We support deletion APIs and can expunge data and embeddings; for Dedicated/Private you control the storage so deletion is immediate per your policy. Hosted can honor deletion requests but we will need the identifiers and may have short backup retention windows; we'll document the flow. 07:58 Sanjay: For long-term archiving of logs for compliance, do you provide immutability (WORM) options? 08:05 Alex: We can integrate with your archival S3 buckets with immutability policies; for Hosted there are standard retention modes, Dedicated/Private give you more control. 08:15 Marta: Ok, procurement wants to see a sample contract clause for data residency and subprocessors. 08:21 Alex: will include sample clauses in the security pack. 08:24 Jenna: One more — PII redaction in transcripts; can Redwood automatically redact SSNs/PANs on ingest? 08:31 Priya: We have regex-based pre-processors and can run PII detection to redact or mask tokens at ingestion. for high assurance, customers often tokenise client-side. 08:42 Tom: Any regulatory certifications for financial services beyond SOC2/ISO? 08:47 Alex: We don't have FI-specific certifications like PCI attestation for processing PANs; we advise tokenization or specialized PCI-compliant processors for PAN. we can support integration patterns. 08:58 Marta: Sounds reasonable. let's talk timeline — procurement review in two weeks, security sign-off following that. 09:05 Alex: Great. we'll send the docs and proposed benchmark timeslots. wrap-up: summarize next steps, owners and due dates. 09:13 Marta: thanks everyone. 09:15 Alex: Thanks, bye.
